text:
## Observations

1. At least one cell is already black, so the minimum and maximum row and column indices of the black cells define a nonempty bounding rectangle.
2. Every valid rectangle must contain the entire bounding rectangle of the already-black cells.
3. If the bounding rectangle contains no fixed white cell, painting every `?` inside it black and every `?` outside it white gives a valid coloring.
4. The bounding rectangle may be a single row, a single column, or a single cell. Its boundaries are inclusive.
5. The grid has \(HW\) cells, and the bounding rectangle is described by four indices.

## Solution sketch

1. “At least one cell is already black, so the minimum and maximum row and column indices of the black cells define a nonempty bounding rectangle.” Read and store the grid while scanning for `#` cells. Track the smallest and largest row and column indices among those cells.
2. “Every valid rectangle must contain the entire bounding rectangle of the already-black cells.” Inspect the cells within the four bounds. If any cell is `.`, print `No`, because every candidate rectangle would have to include that fixed white cell.
3. “The bounding rectangle may be a single row, a single column, or a single cell. Its boundaries are inclusive.” Include both endpoints in each dimension when inspecting the rectangle. This also checks a one-cell grid correctly.
4. “If the bounding rectangle contains no fixed white cell, painting every `?` inside it black and every `?` outside it white gives a valid coloring.” If the inspection finds no `.`, print `Yes`. The coloring only needs to exist, so the program can print the answer without modifying the grid.
5. “The grid has \(HW\) cells, and the bounding rectangle is described by four indices.” The initial scan and the rectangle inspection each visit at most \(HW\) cells, for \(O(HW)\) time. The stored grid uses \(O(HW)\) space, with \(O(1)\) additional working space.

isolation.mechanism: codex exec, fresh ephemeral session, empty temporary working directory, user config and exec rules ignored, read-only sandbox, web search and listed features disabled, credential-like variables removed from the environment
isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
